To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel MnTMPyP-dsdNA complex-guided in situ deposition of PANI was successfully developed for the first time to fabricate an electrochemical biosensing platform for TB assay.

the MnTMPyP-dSDNA complex can catalyze the in situ generation of PANI on a glassy carbon electrode (GCE) by the oxidation of 4-aminoantipyrine (4-AAP) with H2O2, and that the MnTMPpyP-dsDNA/PANI/GCE modified electrode exhibits excellent catalytic activity toward H2O2 and can be employed to develop an ultrasensitive electrochemical biosensor for TB detection.

a MnTMPyP-dSDNA artificial enzyme mimic was successfully constructed and used for the first time to catalyze the oxidation of o-phenylenediamine (OPD) to generate PANI in situ for electrochemical detection of TB, which was achieved by using a novel strategy for the fabrication of an electrochemical sensor based on MnTMPyP- dsDNA and PANI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel electrochemical method for TB sensing by using MnTMPyP-dsdNA as a powerful catalyst to generate PANI on the electrode surface.

the development of an electrochemical strategy for the highly sensitive and selective detection of TB based on the MnTMPyP-dsdNA catalytic peroxidase-like activity and in situ generation of PANI as an efficient electrochemical redox mediator.
the development of a new MnTMPyP-dsdNA complex guided in situ synthesis of PANI as a redox probe for sensitive detection of TB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of MnTMPyP-dsdDNA complex guided in situ generation of PANI is a novel and effective electrochemical method for TB detection with high sensitivity, selectivity, and stability.
the MnTMPyP-dsdNA complex guided the in situ deposition of PANI for electrochemical TB detection.
the proposed method provides a new and facile approach for TB detection with high sensitivity.

MnTMPyP-dsdNA complex guided in situ generation of PANI for electrochemical thrombi detection.

the MnTMPyP-dsdNA complex can be used as a peroxidase-like catalyst to catalyze the oxidation reaction of 4-chlorophenol (4-CP) by hydrogen peroxide (H2O2).
the MnTMPyP-dsdNA complex can be utilized as a peroxidase mimic and template for in situ generation of PANI.
